subject: How a tool quietly became infrastructure
body:
Dear {{officialName}},

A tool gets picked up and put down. Infrastructure runs continuously and shapes what everything around it assumes. Plate readers near {{shortName}} were probably sold as the first sort of thing and have become the second, with a private company as the operator.

Infrastructure decisions deserve a level of deliberation this one does not appear to have had, including public hearings and a documented way to reverse course. I have looked for signs of either and come up short.

What I am asking is that {{city}} treat removal as the correction, taking the readers near campus out and authorizing none to replace them. Would you tell me whether you consider this program infrastructure, and whether it has ever been reviewed as such? I am a student here and would value your view.

subject: Terms that will bind councils not yet elected
body:
Dear {{officialName}},

A long commitment made today constrains the people who will hold your seat later. That is normal for a building and questionable for a surveillance capability, because the political judgment behind it may not survive the term of the agreement.

Future members will inherit the cameras around {{shortName}} along with a relationship the company has every reason to continue. Their room to reconsider will be narrower than yours is now, and that narrowing is what concerns me.

The kindest thing to do for them may be to close it out. I hope you will support removing the plate readers near campus and approving no new ones. Would you tell me how long the current commitment runs and what ending it would require? I am a student here and would be grateful to know.

subject: A written answer on custody before any renewal
body:
Dear {{officialName}},

Nothing in this note requires you to agree with me about surveillance. It asks only that {{city}} be able to say, in writing, who holds the plate data collected around {{shortName}} and under what conditions anyone else can reach it.

If that answer exists, publishing it costs nothing. Should it not exist, then a program running near {{school}} has been operating without anyone establishing the most basic fact about it, and that possibility is what worries me most.

For my part, I would like the readers around campus removed and no new ones installed. Would you seek a written custody answer before any renewal, and would you share it with the student who asked? I would be grateful, whatever the answer turns out to be.

subject: What a genuine audit of this system would need
body:
Dear {{officialName}},

An audit worth the name would need access to raw logs rather than company summaries, and a reviewer the company cannot turn away. Anything less produces a document that reassures without verifying.

My guess is that {{city}} has neither, for the plate readers around {{shortName}} or for anything else on that platform. I would be pleased to be wrong, and I would much rather hear it from you than from a marketing page.

The simpler path is still removal, taking the cameras near campus out of service and installing none in their place. Would you tell me whether {{city}} holds the access a genuine audit would require? I am a student here, and I have asked around without getting close to an answer.

subject: A public decision that ended up inside a contract
body:
Dear {{officialName}},

Strip this issue down and one thing is left. A decision about how closely people in {{city}} are watched now lives inside a commercial arrangement, where the public can neither read the terms nor reach the records.

Everything else follows from that. Whatever the merits of the technology, a function this consequential should not rest with a party answering to customers rather than to residents of {{state}}.

My request is the one I would make to any member of {{role}}, which is to remove the plate readers around {{shortName}} and install no new ones. Would you tell me your position, and whether you will raise the question of custody before the next vote? I am a student here, and I would be grateful for a reply of any length.
